metric_definitions.start_s: when the request was sent, relative to the first request of the run
metric_definitions.client_queue_s: time a request waited in the client for a free concurrency slot before it was sent; not part of any latency below
metric_definitions.ttft_s: time from sending the request to receiving the first output token
metric_definitions.e2e_s: time from sending the request to receiving the last output token
metric_definitions.tpot_s: (e2e_s - ttft_s) / (output_tokens - 1): mean gap between output tokens after the first
metric_definitions.duration_s: last response end minus first request start, from the rows
metric_definitions.output_tok_per_s: sum of output_tokens of completed requests / duration_s
metric_definitions.percentiles: numpy.percentile with linear interpolation over the completed requests of one run (500 in the main matrix)
metric_definitions.burst: the first `concurrency` requests by start time: they are sent together at t=0 and queue behind each other
metric_definitions.peak_in_flight: largest number of requests between send and last token at any instant, from the rows; an end within 1 microsecond of a start counts as before it
metric_definitions.cache_hit_rate: prefix_cache_hits / prefix_cache_queries, both as counter differences between the snapshot after warm-up and the snapshot after the measured requests
metric_definitions.counters: request_success, prompt_tokens, generation_tokens, prefix_cache_queries, prefix_cache_hits, num_preemptions: differences over the measured requests only
metric_definitions.pair_speedup: output_tok_per_s of the cache-on run / output_tok_per_s of the cache-off run of the same pair
metric_definitions.condition_speedup: geometric mean of the pair speedups of a condition (primary metric); min and max of the pairs are reported next to it

validity_rules.requests: every measured and warm-up request completed without error
validity_rules.output_length: every request generated exactly workload.output_len tokens
validity_rules.input_length: every prompt was counted as the expected number of tokens by the client and, in total, by the server
validity_rules.fresh_server: the server had handled no request before the warm-up
validity_rules.counter_window: request_success, prompt_tokens and generation_tokens moved by exactly the measured requests between the two snapshots
validity_rules.cache_hits: with no preemption: cache off gives 0 hit tokens; cache on gives exactly num_prompts x cacheable_tokens_per_request
validity_rules.in_flight: peak_in_flight never exceeds the configured concurrency
validity_rules.timing: 0 < ttft_s <= e2e_s and all numbers are finite
validity_rules.failure: an attempt that breaks a rule is kept and reported as FAILED; it is never averaged in and never skipped by resume
